messages:
Alex (Sales): Heads-up — Renewal for FinFlow is due next week. They used a 3-month POC and want an uplift + longer commit. Asking for a 30% discount on the new rate card. I told them I'd check with deal desk and legal.
Maria (CS): FYI they've been hitting the Dedicated tier and using KV cache extensively. Latency looks stable. We promised a POC price that was below list.
Kiran (SE): POC config: 4xA10g, 8k token avg, batching enabled. Cost per 1M tokens was ~`$620` during POC (with burst credits). If we push them to reserved commit, unit cost should drop.
Alex (Sales): They also submitted the security questionnaire yesterday; Olga, any blockers on the SSO/KMS answers? Customer needs written KMS confirmation for compliance.
Olga (Legal): Haven't reviewed the full SQ yet — can you drop the link? We usually can confirm KMS integrations but not transfer keys. Need to check NDA terms for data residency.
Maria (CS): Link: https://docs.internal/finflow/sq-attachments (shared via private link). They called out audit log retention and dedicated VPC.
Sophie (Deal Desk): 30% off baseline for renewals is pretty aggressive for Dedicated. What's the ARR if they sign a 12-month reserved capacity? Need numbers to model concession.
Alex (Sales): Current ARR w/ POC credits normalized would be about `$180k` annualized at list. With 30% discount they'd be `$126k`. They're asking for 12mo commit + auto-renew.
Kiran (SE): Technical ask: they'll want a canary rollout and fallback to hosted if Dedicated has maintenance. We should include SLOs in the quote. Also recommend a quantization profile to reduce GPU needs by ~15%.
Sophie (Deal Desk): Ok — two levers we can offer instead of straight %: 1) 12mo commit at 15% + 2 months free, or 2) 20% off with a usage-based rebate structure. Both preserve margin better. Which does CS prefer?
Maria (CS): Option 1 is easier for ops — predictable capacity. Option 2 might be nicer for their finance team. They asked specifically for simple net reduction though.
Olga (Legal): If we add auto-renew + credits we must update Term Exhibit and include termination rights. I'll need 48h to draft. No problem on KMS statement — we can confirm supported integrations and that keys remain customer-managed.
Dave (SRE): From infra POV, Dedicated + VPC + audit retention is fine. We need 2-week lead time for provisioning and a maintenance window SLA. We'll add a note: `Provisioning ETA: 14 days` and `SLA: 99.5%` in the quote.
Alex (Sales): Sophie, can you run the margin calc for both concession options and flag any internal approvals required? Also, they asked for a one-off data portability clause in the contract.
Sophie (Deal Desk): On it. I'll run numbers and loop in finance if the blended margin goes below our floor. Expect a decision thread by EOD tomorrow. @Olga please include the portability clause language you're okay with.
Olga (Legal): Draft portability clause: "Customer can export model artifacts and logs within 30 days of termination; Redwood will provide export tooling per documented APIs. Charges may apply for large exports." Will refine.
Kiran (SE): For the POC -> Prod handover, I'll prepare a short runbook and include recommended quant and batching profiles. I can attach a sample config snippet: 
```
batching: on
quantization: int8
max_seq: 8192
autoscale: policy:reserve:4
```
Maria (CS): Customer meeting Thursday at 10am PT to discuss pricing options and security updates. I've tentatively scheduled it.
Alex (Sales): Great. Sophie — if you can pre-approve the 15% + 2 months option for AE signoff, it would speed closure. If not, we'll escalate.
Sophie (Deal Desk): I can pre-approve up to 18% for 12mo if finance signs off on the estimated ARR. If they still ask 30% we'll need exec review.
Alex (Sales): Thanks all. I'll prep the quote with Option A and B and include Olga's portability note + Dave's provisioning ETA. Meeting notes + draft quote will be posted after the call. :thumbsup:
